t: How to Use Quizzes in Thrive Apprentice
c:
In this article, you'll learn how to integrate Thrive Quiz Builder quizzes into your Thrive Apprentice courses. You'll cover the "Mark as Complete" feature, gating lesson progression behind quiz results, enrolling students after quiz completion, unlocking content after a final exam, and customizing the completion notification message.

Why Use Quizzes in Your Courses?

Adding quizzes to your Thrive Apprentice courses lets you verify that students understand the material before they move on. Quizzes can serve as knowledge checks within lessons, gates that control progression, or even entry requirements for course enrollment. Thrive Quiz Builder provides the quiz functionality, and Thrive Apprentice handles the course progression logic.

Using the "Mark as Complete" Feature on a Quiz

The Mark as Complete feature lets students indicate they've finished a lesson. When you add a quiz to a lesson, you can tie this button directly to quiz completion—so students can only mark the lesson as done after they've taken the quiz.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0fAZhli9QGk

Here's how to set it up:

  1. Navigate to Thrive Dashboard > Thrive Apprentice and open the course you want to edit.
  2. Select the lesson that contains your quiz.
  3. Open the lesson settings and locate the Completion section.
  4. Set the Mark as Complete behavior to require quiz completion.
  5. Save your changes.

Once configured, the Mark Lesson as Complete button will remain inactive until the student finishes the quiz. This keeps your progress tracking accurate and ensures students engage with the assessment before continuing.

Enabling "Mark as Complete" Only After the User Passes the Quiz

You can take the previous setup one step further by requiring students to not just complete the quiz, but actually pass it with a minimum score. This prevents students who fail from advancing to the next lesson.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WEAgBQf33jQ
  1. Navigate to Thrive Dashboard > Thrive Apprentice and open your course.
  2. Select the lesson with the quiz.
  3. In the lesson's Completion settings, set the behavior to Quiz must be passed.
  4. Define the passing score threshold in Thrive Quiz Builder (e.g., 70% or higher).
  5. Save your settings.

Now, only students who meet or exceed the passing score will see the Mark Lesson as Complete button become active. Students who score below the threshold can retake the quiz until they pass.

Tip: Set a clear passing threshold that reflects the difficulty of the material. A score between 70% and 80% is common for most educational courses.

Unlocking the Next Lesson Only After a Student Passes the Quiz

Beyond controlling the Mark as Complete button, you can lock subsequent lessons behind quiz results using Thrive Apprentice's drip and scheduling features. This ensures students truly master each section before accessing the next one.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=oojQhn4spVU
  1. Navigate to Thrive Dashboard > Thrive Apprentice and open your course.
  2. Go to Courses in the sidebar and select your course.
  3. Add your quiz to the lesson content using Thrive Quiz Builder.
  4. Open the Drip settings for the course.
  5. Create a new Drip Schedule and set the unlock condition to After previous lesson is completed.
  6. Link the drip schedule to your course's product under the Access Restrictions settings.
  7. Save and publish.

With this configuration, the next lesson in the sequence only becomes available after the student completes (and passes, if required) the current lesson's quiz. This creates a linear, mastery-based learning path.

Enrolling Users in a Course After They Complete a Quiz

You can use a standalone quiz as a gateway to course enrollment. For example, you might offer a free assessment on your website and automatically enroll anyone who completes it into a course. This workflow uses Thrive Automator to connect Thrive Quiz Builder with Thrive Apprentice.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=r9pBH3FpjDM
  1. Create your quiz in Thrive Quiz Builder and add a WordPress account connection to the quiz's opt-in gate. This ensures quiz takers are registered as WordPress users.
  2. Go to Thrive Dashboard > Thrive Automator and click + Add New.
  3. Set the Start Trigger to User completes quiz.
  4. Select the specific quiz from the dropdown.
  5. Add an Action and select Grant access to product.
  6. Choose the Thrive Apprentice product that contains the course you want to enroll them in.
  7. Click Save and Activate.

Important: The quiz must have an active WordPress account connection in its opt-in gate. Without this, quiz takers won't have WordPress accounts, and the automation won't be able to grant them course access.

Unlocking Lesson Content After Students Pass the Final Exam

If your course includes a final exam, you can unlock bonus content, certificates, or additional resources only after a student passes it. This uses a combination of Thrive Automator and Thrive Apprentice's drip feature.

  1. Create the final exam quiz in Thrive Quiz Builder with a defined passing score.
  2. In Thrive Apprentice, add the bonus content as a separate lesson or module that is initially locked.
  3. Set up a Drip Schedule with an unlock condition tied to quiz completion.
  4. Go to Thrive Dashboard > Thrive Automator and create an automation where: - Start Trigger: User completes quiz (select your final exam) - Filter: Score meets the passing threshold - Action: Grant access to the locked content or update the student's progress
  5. Save and activate the automation.

This approach rewards students who complete the entire course and pass the final assessment, motivating them to engage thoroughly with your material.

Changing the "Mark Lesson as Complete" Notification Message

When students interact with the Mark Lesson as Complete button—especially when it's tied to a quiz—they see a notification message. You can customize this message to match your brand voice or provide specific instructions.

  1. Navigate to Thrive Dashboard > Thrive Apprentice.
  2. Open the course and select the lesson whose notification you want to change.
  3. Go to the lesson's Completion settings.
  4. Locate the Notification Message field.
  5. Edit the text to display your preferred message. For example, you might change it from the default to something like "Great job! You've passed the quiz. Click below to continue to the next lesson."
  6. Save your changes.

You can set different messages depending on the quiz outcome:

  • Passed: A congratulatory message with instructions to proceed.
  • Failed: An encouraging message prompting the student to review the material and retake the quiz.
  • Completed (no pass/fail): A neutral confirmation message.

Tip: Keep notification messages short, positive, and actionable. Students should immediately understand what to do next.

Conclusion

That's it! You've successfully learned how to integrate quizzes into your Thrive Apprentice courses using Thrive Quiz Builder. From simple completion tracking to advanced enrollment automations, quizzes give you powerful tools to create structured, mastery-based learning experiences for your students.

t: How to Enable Assessments in Thrive Apprentice
c:
In this article, you'll learn how to enable and configure assessments in Thrive Apprentice. Assessments let you evaluate student work beyond multiple-choice quizzes—students can upload files, submit video links, share external URLs, or complete traditional quiz-based evaluations.

What Are Assessments?

Assessments are a feature introduced in Thrive Apprentice version 5.8 that gives you flexible ways to evaluate student progress. Unlike quizzes that are automatically graded, assessments support manual review by the instructor—making them ideal for essays, projects, presentations, and other hands-on assignments.

Thrive Apprentice supports four assessment submission types:

  • Quiz: Traditional quiz-based assessments using Thrive Quiz Builder with automated grading.
  • Upload: Students submit files such as documents, PDFs, presentations, or images.
  • YouTube Link: Students provide a YouTube video URL—perfect for video presentations, demonstrations, or recorded assignments.
  • External Link: Students share a URL to work hosted on another platform (e.g., Google Docs, portfolio sites, or code repositories).

Prerequisites

Before enabling assessments, make sure you have:

  • Thrive Apprentice version 5.8 or later installed and activated
  • At least one published course with lessons
  • For upload-type assessments, an API connection to Google Drive or Dropbox (see the assessment upload settings guide)

How to Enable Assessments for a Course

  1. Navigate to Thrive Dashboard > Thrive Apprentice.
  2. Click Courses in the left sidebar and select the course you want to add assessments to.
  3. Open the lesson or module where you want to add an assessment.
  4. In the lesson editor, locate the Assessment section.
  5. Toggle the Enable Assessment switch to turn it on.
  6. Select the Assessment Type from the dropdown: - Quiz — link an existing Thrive Quiz Builder quiz - Upload — allow file submissions - YouTube Link — accept YouTube video URLs - External Link — accept external URLs
  7. Configure any additional settings specific to your chosen type (e.g., passing score for quizzes, allowed file types for uploads).
  8. Click Save to apply your changes.

Note: You can add assessments to individual lessons, modules, or as a final course-level evaluation. The placement depends on how you want to structure your grading.

How Students Submit Assessments

Once assessments are enabled, students will see a submission area within the lesson page. The submission process depends on the assessment type:

  1. The student opens the lesson that contains the assessment.
  2. They scroll to the Assessment section at the bottom of the lesson content.
  3. Depending on the type, they either: - Complete the embedded quiz - Upload a file using the Upload button - Paste a YouTube video URL into the provided field - Enter an external link in the URL field
  4. They click Submit Assessment to send their work for review.

After submission, the student sees a confirmation message. They can view their submission status—Pending, Passed, or Failed—from their course dashboard.

Instructor Review Workflow

As the instructor, you review and grade non-quiz assessments manually. Here's how:

  1. Navigate to Thrive Dashboard > Thrive Apprentice.
  2. Click Assessments in the left sidebar to see all pending submissions.
  3. Select a submission to review the student's work.
  4. Review the uploaded file, video, or linked content.
  5. Choose a result: Pass or Fail.
  6. Optionally, add feedback comments for the student.
  7. Click Save to finalize the grade.

The student will be notified of the result, and their course progress will update accordingly. If the assessment is required for lesson completion, the student won't be able to proceed until they receive a passing grade.

Tip: Review assessments regularly to keep students moving through your course. Delayed reviews can frustrate learners and lead to drop-offs.

Conclusion

That's it! You've successfully learned how to enable assessments in Thrive Apprentice. With four flexible submission types and a built-in review workflow, assessments give you the tools to evaluate real student work—not just quiz answers.

t: How to Manage Assessment Upload Settings in Thrive Apprentice
c:
In this article, you'll learn how to configure the upload settings for assessments in Thrive Apprentice. This includes connecting a cloud storage service, selecting allowed file types, setting size limits, and managing student submissions through the review process.

Why You Need Upload Settings

When you enable upload-type assessments, students submit files directly through your course. Those files need a storage destination. Thrive Apprentice integrates with Google Drive and Dropbox to securely store submitted files, so you'll need an active API connection with one of these services before students can upload anything.

Prerequisites

Before configuring upload settings, make sure you have:

  • Thrive Apprentice version 5.8 or later
  • Assessments enabled for at least one lesson (see How to Enable Assessments)
  • A Google Drive or Dropbox account ready for API connection

Step 1: Connect Your Cloud Storage Service

  1. Navigate to Thrive Dashboard > Thrive Apprentice.
  2. Click Settings in the left sidebar.
  3. Locate the Assessment Uploads section.
  4. Click Connect Service and choose either Google Drive or Dropbox.
  5. Follow the on-screen prompts to authorize Thrive Apprentice to access your cloud storage account.
  6. Once connected, you'll see a confirmation message with the connected service name.

Note: For detailed instructions on setting up the Google Drive or Dropbox API connection, refer to the respective API connection guides in the Thrive Apprentice knowledge base.

Step 2: Configure File Type and Size Limits

After connecting your storage service, you can control what students are allowed to upload:

  1. In the Assessment Uploads section, locate the Allowed File Types setting.
  2. Select the file extensions you want to accept. Common options include: - Documents: .pdf, .doc, .docx, .txt - Spreadsheets: .xls, .xlsx, .csv - Presentations: .ppt, .pptx - Images: .jpg, .png, .gif - Archives: .zip
  3. Set the Maximum File Size limit. Choose a value that accommodates your expected submissions without overloading your storage (e.g., 10 MB, 25 MB, or 50 MB).
  4. Click Save to apply the settings.

Tip: If you're accepting video or large project files, consider using the YouTube Link or External Link assessment types instead. These avoid large file uploads while still letting students share their work.

Step 3: Choose a Storage Destination Folder

  1. In the Assessment Uploads section, click Select Folder.
  2. Browse your connected Google Drive or Dropbox account and choose the folder where you want student submissions stored.
  3. Click Confirm to set the destination.

All student uploads will be saved to this folder. Thrive Apprentice organizes files by course and student name, making it easy to locate specific submissions.

Managing Student Submissions

Once students begin submitting assessments, you can manage their uploads from the Thrive Apprentice dashboard:

  1. Navigate to Thrive Dashboard > Thrive Apprentice > Assessments.
  2. You'll see a list of all submissions with their current status: Pending, Passed, or Failed.
  3. Click on any submission to open the review panel.
  4. From the review panel, you can: - View or download the uploaded file directly from your connected cloud storage - Mark as Passed or Mark as Failed - Add feedback comments for the student
  5. Click Save to finalize the review.

Important: Students cannot proceed past an assessment-gated lesson until you review their submission and assign a passing grade. Make sure to check the Assessments panel regularly.

Troubleshooting Common Issues

  • Upload button is grayed out: The cloud storage API connection is missing or expired. Reconnect your Google Drive or Dropbox under Settings > Assessment Uploads.
  • File rejected on upload: The student's file type or size exceeds the limits you configured. Adjust the settings or ask the student to compress/convert their file.
  • Files not appearing in storage: Verify the destination folder still exists and that the API connection has the correct permissions.

Conclusion

That's it! You've successfully configured assessment upload settings in Thrive Apprentice. With cloud storage connected and file limits in place, your students can submit their work and you can review it—all from within your WordPress dashboard.

Related Resources

  • Google Drive API setup: Connecting Google Drive to Thrive Apprentice
  • Dropbox API setup: Connecting Dropbox to Thrive Apprentice

t: How to Refresh Templates in Thrive Apprentice After Adding Assessments
c:
In this article, you'll learn why you need to refresh your Thrive Apprentice templates after adding assessments, which templates require updating, and how to complete the process in just a few clicks.

Why Templates Need Refreshing

If you created and designed your Thrive Apprentice course before enabling assessments, your existing templates don't include the layout elements needed to display assessment content. The lesson list template, for example, won't show assessment items, and the assessment template itself won't exist yet in your design.

Refreshing your templates adds the necessary data structures and layout components so that assessments appear correctly on the front end of your site.

Note: If you're building a brand-new course and enabling assessments from the start, you can skip this step. The templates will already include assessment support when you first design them.

When You'll See the Refresh Notice

After you enable assessments for a lesson in an existing course, Thrive Apprentice will display a notice prompting you to reload your templates. You may see this notice in the course editor or when viewing the course on the front end. The message typically asks you to "reload the lesson list template" to reflect the newly added assessment content.

Don't ignore this notice—until you refresh, assessments won't appear for your students even though they're enabled in the backend.

Which Templates Need Refreshing

Two templates require updates:

  • Lesson List Template: This template displays the list of lessons within a course or module. After adding assessments, it needs to be refreshed so that assessment items appear alongside regular lessons in the course structure.
  • Assessment Template: This template controls how the assessment submission area looks on the lesson page. Refreshing creates this template if it doesn't already exist in your design.

How to Refresh Your Templates

  1. Navigate to Thrive Dashboard > Thrive Apprentice.
  2. Open the course where you've added assessments.
  3. Look for the template refresh notice at the top of the page or in the course editor.
  4. Click the Refresh Templates button (or Reload Lesson List Template, depending on the notice).
  5. Wait a few seconds for Thrive Apprentice to update the templates.
  6. Once complete, you'll see a confirmation that the templates have been refreshed.
  7. Preview your course on the front end to verify that assessments now appear correctly in the lesson list and on individual lesson pages.

Important: Refreshing templates does not delete your existing design or content. It adds the assessment-related elements to your current template structure. Your lesson layouts, styling, and other customizations remain intact.

What Changes After Refreshing

After the refresh, you'll notice the following changes:

  • Assessment items appear in the lesson list alongside regular lessons.
  • The assessment submission area (upload button, link field, or quiz embed) displays on the appropriate lesson pages.
  • Students can see their assessment status (Pending, Passed, Failed) in the course overview.

If you've customized your templates extensively using Thrive Architect, review the refreshed templates to make sure the new assessment elements fit your design. You can adjust the layout and styling of assessment components just like any other Thrive Architect element.

Conclusion

That's it! You've successfully refreshed your Thrive Apprentice templates to support assessments. This quick step ensures that your students can see and interact with assessments on the front end of your course.
